definition.title: Healthy-adult pulmonary 0D structural candidate with pressure-distensible resistance vessels

baseline_cardiac_output.derivation: The locked MEHLISSA reference is 6 L/min within the published healthy resting interval.

left_atrial_pressure.derivation: Eight mmHg is the locked nominal pressure sink; measured PAWP may replace it as an external boundary.

pulmonary_vascular_resistance.derivation: The 1.2 WU value is retained as the observable secant PVR at the reference flow and pressure. For v5 it is not R0: the Linehan zero-pressure resistance is derived so that this reference equilibrium is preserved exactly.

pulmonary_arterial_compliance.derivation: The locked 5 mL/mmHg arterial compliance is retained for mean-pressure relaxation; resistance-vessel distensibility is a separate mechanical quantity.

pulmonary_transit_time.derivation: The measured healthy-control resting first-pass transit reference is retained without an exercise rule.

right_lung_perfusion_fraction.derivation: The source-derived supine RPA/(RPA+LPA) split is retained; regional redistribution remains outside v5.

mean_pulmonary_arterial_pressure_target.derivation: The derived R0 normalization makes the default 55-year reference equilibrium exactly 15.2 mmHg at 6 L/min and 8 mmHg left-atrial pressure.

minimum_supported_age_years.derivation: Lower boundary of the directly applicable invasive resting-PVR stratum.

older_lower_age_years.derivation: Boundary of the pooled 60-and-older resistance band.

maximum_supported_age_years.derivation: Upper boundary of the reported healthy-adult age range.

young_resistance_multiplier.derivation: Invasive 0.8625 WU divided by the locked 1.2 WU reference; limited to ages 24-under-40.

older_resistance_multiplier.derivation: Published age-stratum PASP/CO ratio relative to the 40-59 reference band.

reference_cardiac_output.derivation: The R0 normalization is anchored at the locked 6 L/min MEHLISSA resting flow.

reference_left_atrial_pressure.derivation: The R0 normalization is anchored at the locked 8 mmHg nominal pressure sink.

coefficient.derivation: The healthy human mean alpha 0.020 +/- 0.002 mmHg^-1 is converted to SI by division by 133.322387415 Pa/mmHg. The Linehan fifth-power equation converts pressure-dependent vessel diameter into the nonlinear mean pressure-flow relation.

validity.population: healthy adults aged 24-85 represented by the retained age-conditioned resistance levels and a healthy-human mean distensibility coefficient
validity.physiological_state: fully recruited zone-3 mean pulmonary circulation from rest through exercise with measured PAWP permitted as a boundary
validity.description: Structural mean-flow candidate using the Linehan fifth-power distensible-vessel equation. Observable reference PVR is normalized to a derived zero-pressure resistance; fixed arterial compliance supplies first-order pressure relaxation.

limitations: This is a research structural candidate, not a diagnostic or treatment model.
Linehan 1992 established the equation in isolated dog lung lobes; Reeves 2005 supplies the human exercise calibration of alpha.
The equation assumes fully recruited zone-3 resistance vessels, constant hematocrit, one alpha throughout the vascular bed, and mean rather than pulsatile flow.
The empirical Claessen resistance power law is deliberately absent to prevent double-counting the exercise-related fall in apparent PVR.
The fixed arterial compliance controls transient mean pressure but is not the same quantity as resistance-vessel diameter distensibility.
The healthy-human mean alpha is held constant even though Reeves reported a tendency to lower values in men over 60 years; age-conditioned alpha is deferred pending a separately qualified rule.
The zero-pressure resistance R0 is a model quantity derived at runtime, not the observed resting PVR and not a directly measured parameter.
PAWP is a surrogate for left-atrial pressure and low-flow derecruitment or critical-closing-pressure behavior is outside the fully recruited model.
Transit time and right/left perfusion remain fixed during exercise.
Gas exchange, biochemical exchange, lobar recruitment, autoregulation, disease, sex-specific alpha, and patient anatomy are outside v5.
